prerequisites: Euclidian/Cartesian geometry and mathematical functions (algebraic and differential)

learning_outcomes.text: Modelling methods and techniques, virtual prototyping and product plan development for an industrial product, CAD modelling, modelling methods and representation schemes.
Digital Human Modelling in Human Centred Design, ergonomics and comfort evaluation.
Alphabet and language for virtual prototyping and for 2D and 3D virtual design.
Knowledge of the latest PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) techniques.
Be skilled in modelling in 3D CAD and in DHM environments.
Be skilled to model and analyze an interaction between humans and artefacts.
Be skilled about mathematical functions underlying the DHM and the CAD modelers.
Be able to individuate most appropriate methods for designing and improving an industrial product/process.
Be able to make the better choice among commercial software in virtual design in terms of efficiency and effectiveness.
Be able to work in group and to explain and present with the right language (specific terms and words) a topic inherent to virtual design ones.
To be able to develop a design process by using the right hardware/software and to know the right nouns in Italian and English language.
To be able to apply and use the acquired knowledge in different frameworks and to apply the methods and the techniques in other field of study/research/application.

syllabus_topics: Innovation and prototyping (meanings of words, explanations, history and evolution, product development and innovation)
Computer Aided Design ("computer aided" technologies in product development plan for time-to-market improvement and cut)
CAD-CAXX techniques (CAD-model based design techniques, CAD-CAM, CAD-CAE, CAD-CAPP, CAXX, DHM)
PLM (the product design and the management of its lifecycle; Product Data Management, Customer Relationship Management, Enterprise Resource Planning)
Computer Aided Design topics (modelling domains and representation domains)
Modelling and representation (modelling techniques and representation schemes. Application to virtual prototyping)
CAD mathematical functions (parametric curves and surfaces, approximating curves' and surfaces' functions)
User Centred Design and Human Centred Design
Ergonomics and Comfort (ergonomics principles, product and process ergonomic evaluation, product and process comfort evaluation, workplaces analysis)
teaching_methods: Laboratory experience about instruments for acquiring data for ergonomics/comfort analysis
Development of an assigned project in group with brain-storming techniques and like-company structured team working
assessment_rules: Marks are in thirtieths. 18/30 is given to students showing sufficient knowledge and competence in project discussion and able to answer three of five questions during the oral exam. 30/30 is given to students showing complete knowledge and competence in project discussion and able to answer all five questions. 30 cum laude is awarded for a very high preparation level, high technical language skills (also in English), and self-deepening of topics regarding CAD mathematical modelling and representation.
